gist: The annual Orionid meteor shower is returning to the night sky this week.
Earth passes through debris from Halley's Comet, creating fast-moving streaks of light.
Peak viewing occurs overnight between October 21 and 22, with mixed weather forecasts.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Earth is passing through debris left by Halley's Comet, causing the annual Orionid meteor shower to become active. Tiny particles enter the atmosphere at high speed and create visible streaks of light across the night sky.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is one of the best-known meteor showers of the year, offering viewers a chance to see up to twenty meteors per hour under ideal conditions without needing any special equipment.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The shower will reach its peak overnight from October 21 to 22. Observers should look between midnight and dawn from dark locations, though cloud cover and moonlight may affect visibility in some areas.
